title: International Honeymoon Itinerary with Flight Cancellation Cascade

scenario.description: Newlyweds planned a 10-day romantic honeymoon across three European cities: Paris, Venice, and Barcelona. A flight cancellation in the middle of the trip forces complete itinerary restructuring.

dynamic_events.description: Your Paris → Venice connecting flight on June 18 has been cancelled due to mechanical issues. The airline offers two options: (1) Rebook you on a flight departing June 19 at 7 AM (losing one full day in Venice), or (2) Route you through Rome on June 18 evening, arriving Venice June 19 at 11 PM (exhausting arrival). Any rebooking costs an additional $400 per ticket (total $800). You must also decide whether to keep or cancel your current Venice hotel checkout on June 19.
resolution_requirements: Choose between two flight options (losing a day vs exhausting evening arrival)
Adjust Venice hotel stay: extend by 1 night OR keep same dates with late arrival
Adjust Barcelona hotel checkin to align with new Venice checkout
If extending Venice hotel, verify new total cost stays within $11000 budget
If choosing Rome routing (option 2), verify $800 surcharge fits budget
Preserve Paris hotel and outbound/return international flights
Ensure all three cities are still visited (required)

expected_challenges: Cascading impact: single flight cancellation affects 4 components (two hotel checkout/checkins, connecting flight timing, budget)
Must choose between sub-optimal solutions (lose vacation day vs exhausting arrival)
Budget pressure: surcharge may force downgrades elsewhere
Must preserve intericity flight connections while adjusting hotel dates
Honeymoon experience quality should be maintained despite the disruption
notes: HARD task because: (1) Three destination cities with linear dependencies, (2) Single disruption cascades to 4 components, (3) International logistics with no direct solutions, (4) Budget pressure creates secondary constraints, (5) Quality/experience considerations beyond just logistics.
